CANTONMENT AREAS UNION COMMITTEES (APPEAL) RULES, 1966
CANTONMENT AREAS UNION COMMITTEES
(APPEAL) RULES, 1966
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 21st May,
1966]
S.R.O. 463(K)/66.--In exercise of the powers conferred by Article
89 of the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 (President's Order 18 of 1959), read
with entry 23 of the Sixth Schedule thereto, the Central Government is pleased
to make the following rules, namely:--
1. Short title, commencement and application.---(1)
These rules may be called the Cantonment Areas Union Committees (Appeal) Rules,
1966,
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
(3) They shall apply to all
appeals preferred from orders passed under the Basic Democracies Order, 1959,
except the appeals preferred by the servants of the Union Committee in matters
relating to the conditions of their service.
2. Appellate Authority.---Save as Otherwise
provided an appeal from an original order passed under the Basic Democracies
Order, 1959, shall lie---
(i) in the case of an order passed
by a Union Committee or its Chairman to the Controlling Authority;
(ii) in the case
of an order passed by an officer or servant of a Union Committee or any other
person who has been authorized in this behalf or, to whom the powers have been
delegated by a Union Committee or its Chairman, to the Chairman of the Union
Committee.
3. Limitation.---The period within which
an appeal under these rules may be preferred shall be thirty days from the date
of the order appealed from:
Provided that in
computing the said period of limitation, the time requisite for obtaining a
copy of the order appealed from shall be excluded:
Provided further
that an appeal may be admitted after the said period of limitation when the
appellant satisfies the preferring of appeal within the said period.
4. Manner of filing appeals.---(1) Every
appeal shall be preferred in the form of a memorandum and shall be presented to
the appellate authority or an officer authorized by it in this behalf, by the
appellant personally or his authorized agent or be sent to such authority by
registered post.
(2) Every memorandum of appeal
shall be in writing and shall set forth concisely the grounds of objections to
the order appealed from and such grounds shall be numbered consecutively.
(3) Every memorandum of appeal
shall be signed and verified by the appellant and shall, unless the authority
before which the appeal is filed dispenses with such requirement, be
accompanied by a certified copy of the order appealed from.
5. Appeal Register--Every appeal received by an appellate authority
shall be entered in a register in the form appended to these rules.
6. Interim order.---The appellate
authority may issue an interim order staying the execution of the order
appealed from where, in its opinion, such execution is likely to materially
affect the relief sought for by the appellant.
7. Hearing of appeal.---(1) The appellate
authority shall give an opportunity to the appellant of being heard in person
or through his recognized agent, if so desired by him.
(2) Unless the appellate
authority decides to dismiss the appeal, it shall issue notice to the authority
which passed the order appealed from and shall take into consideration any representation
that may be made by that authority in respect of th9 matter under appeal.
(3) The appellate authority may,
before deciding the appeal call for the record of the case from the authority
from whose order the appeal is preferred and may cause such enquiry to be made
or obtain such advice, as it may consider necessary.
(4) The appellate authority may
determine the costs of the appeal and specify the party by and to whom such
costs shall be paid.
(5) The decision of the appellate
authority shall be communicated to the appellant and the authority which passed
the order appealed from.
8. Effect of appeal.---The Union Committee
concerned shall give effect to the order passed by the appellate authority.
